div_kart.t: No wings, no gearbox to speak of, no aids of any kind. A kart is the purest thing anybody will ever drive and it is merciless about it.
Everything you are watching here is the driver. There is nothing in a kart to hide behind and nothing to blame.
The chassis IS the suspension in one of these - it flexes, and the driver has to load it deliberately. It is a skill that never leaves you.
Half the Formula One grid learned to race in something like this, and most of them will tell you it was the hardest racing they ever did.
Slipstreaming matters enormously at this level. There is so little power that a tow is worth more than any overtaking move.
You steer a kart with the throttle as much as the wheel. Get it wrong and you are simply a passenger.

div_f4.t: Formula 4 is a driver's category by design - identical cars, a sealed engine, and nothing at all to buy your way past somebody with.
This is the first proper single-seater most of them have driven. Wings, slicks and downforce, all new in the same season.
About a hundred and sixty horsepower and very little aerodynamic grip, which means it rewards being smooth rather than brave.
There is no team advantage to find here. The cars are the same and the results are the driver, which is the whole point of the category.
F4 is where a driver finds out whether he can work with an engineer, and that turns out to matter as much as the lap time.

div_f3.t: Formula 3 is the first category where the aerodynamics really matter. Following closely costs you, and learning that is half the season.
These are quick cars now - a serious step from F4 - and the field is deep enough that a tenth is worth five places.
Everybody on this grid is being watched by somebody. F3 is where junior programmes make up their minds.
Spec chassis, spec engine, and a grid that arrives within a second of each other. There is nowhere for a bad weekend to hide.
The tyre is the thing at this level. Get temperature into it on the out lap or the first flying lap is gone.

div_f2.t: Formula 2 is the last step, and everybody here knows it. One seat above this, and not many of them.
These are heavy, powerful cars with a turbo and a lot of downforce - much closer to a Formula One car than anything below.
The tyre management in this category is brutal, and it is deliberate: it is the skill Formula One most wants to see.
A driver who wins Formula 2 usually gets a chance. Below that it depends entirely on who is watching him and what they were promised.
Reverse grids and a sprint race mean a bad Saturday can be recovered and a good one can be squandered. It rewards a cool head.

div_f1.t: This is the top of the sport. Everything below it exists to find the twenty people who get to be here.
There is no next category. Whatever a driver has left to prove, he proves it in this car or not at all.
The margins here are absurd - a tenth separates a good car from a great one, and a great one from a championship.

div_hatch.t: Front-wheel drive, a sealed engine and no downforce worth the name. It is close, cheap racing and it is where a great many careers start.
Nobody out here is being paid to do this, and every one of them has paid to be here. That changes how a man races.
These cars lift an inside rear through the quick corners, which looks alarming and is entirely normal.
Contact is part of this category. The cars are built expecting it and the drivers race accordingly.
